---
title: Performance Factory
description: Detect latency and error-rate regressions, investigate them with agents, and verify the fix after deploy.
---

The Performance Factory turns a production regression into a tracked task that
agents investigate, fix and verify, with a human approval before anything
ships. It works best when the cause is clear and the fix is contained; broad
redesigns go to an owner instead.

## Pieces

| Piece | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Detector | `scripts/perf/perf-regression-detector.mjs` (apps in `scripts/perf/perf-apps.json`) |
| Investigation procedure | `plugins/tuturuuu/skills/tuturuuu-rollout-recovery/references/perf-forensics.md` |
| Workflow config and stage prompts | `plugins/tuturuuu/skills/tuturuuu-rollout-recovery/references/perf-factory/` |
| Task store | Tuturuuu Tasks **Fleet** board, mirrored to `tmp/perf-factory/tasks/` |
| Backtests | `references/perf-factory/backtests.md` and `scripts/perf/fixtures/` |

## Detector

The detector reads Cloudflare GraphQL analytics for each gateway-mounted app
(`tuturuuu.com/<app>` and its locale-prefixed paths) in rolling windows, 15
minutes by default:

- **Latency:** p95 TTFB per window against the median of the previous 24 hours.
  A window breaches when p95 exceeds `min(1.25 x baseline, baseline + 150 ms)`;
  a regression needs two consecutive breaching windows.
- **Errors:** any single window with at least 5 server errors and a rate at
  least double the baseline and 0.5 percentage points above it.
- Windows with fewer than 50 requests are ignored.

Each regression record names the app, metric, start time, baseline, trigger,
observed values, suspect Worker deployments (with SHAs from version
annotations), a per-version summary, and **reproducible queries**: the GraphQL
text and variables, plus a `rerun` command. Records never hold raw rows.

```bash
node scripts/perf/perf-regression-detector.mjs --apps forms,tools \
  --out tmp/perf-factory/detections/latest.json
node scripts/perf/perf-regression-detector.mjs rerun \
  --record tmp/perf-factory/detections/latest.json --query worker-versions
```

It needs `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Analytics and Workers read),
`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` in the environment and never
prints them. Exit code 2 means configuration or API failure. `--fixture`
replays a recorded series for backtests.

## Workflow

1. **Detect:** a scheduled dispatcher runs the detector every 30 minutes and
   opens or updates a `perf:` task on the Fleet board.
2. **Investigate:** a builder agent follows perf forensics and stores
   hypotheses, evidence and reproducible queries in the task record.
3. **Review the diagnosis:** a fresh-context reviewer on a different provider
   reruns the decisive queries, looks for gaps and tests alternative
   explanations. It may send the task back up to twice.
4. **Propose a fix:** the builder makes the smallest contained fix with a
   regression test in its own worktree, without pushing.
5. **Review the fix:** a fresh-context reviewer rejects over-complex fixes and
   stale-cache hazards and confirms the test fails before and passes after.
6. **Human approval:** the task waits in **Needs User / Review**.
7. **Verify after deploy:** once the fix is live and two windows have closed,
   a verifier reruns the stored query. It closes the task if p95 is back under
   the original trigger, and reopens the investigation otherwise.

Stages that wait on outside events (approval, deploy, closed windows) are
subscriptions the dispatcher checks on each tick. The dispatcher notifies a
person only when a fix is ready for approval or recovery is verified.

A daily agent-log review groups recurring tool and permission failures across
fleet threads and opens `tooling:` fix tasks on the same board.

## Coverage limits

The detector watches Cloudflare-served apps. Vercel-hosted `apps/web`, the
Supabase query side and Flutter startup are covered by the investigation
procedure, not by automatic detection. Deploy-time rejections, such as the
Vercel routing-rule limit, need their own intake from failed production deploy
runs.
